 Pressure (M) film review
 Luke McWilliams 
 November 14, 2026 
 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Email Copy URL 
 In 1944, at the height of the Second World War, a beach is littered with the bodies of troops following a doomed rehearsal for D-Day under General Dwight D. Eisenhower (Brendan Fraser). Six weeks later, Eisenhower schedules the Allied invasion of German-occupied Europe for 5 June in Normandy, France. Soon, Scottish meteorologist Group Captain James Stagg (Andrew Scott) is summoned by Eisenhower to provide a favourable weather forecast for Allied operations on D-Day, which is set to begin in 61 hours…
 A number of movies have been set around D-Day, with Saving Private Ryan (1998) being the most visceral and affecting. With all the elements and variables to consider in any war-related activity, weather patterns seem to be a peculiar, and perhaps even irrelevant, consideration. Not so, as we learn here. Leading the British-US team tasked with providing a forecast using current meteorological intelligence, Capt. Stagg goes head-to-head with Col. Krick, who leads the US section of the team with his analogue forecasting based on historical weather patterns.
 The office environments are lush and extremely detailed. Like The Imitation Game (2014), the mainly male cast of characters live in dark, brown offices surrounded by their implements as they focus on their high-stakes mission. The sets, costumes and mapping props are all incredibly authentic, transporting the audience back to a specific time of high stress and uncertainty.
 Verdict: A solid wartime drama in the mould of Darkest Hour (2017) and Dunkirk (2017). 4 stars.
 Luke McWilliams. themovieclub.net . Viewed at Dendy Cinemas.
